text:
MPC climbed 2.05% today to $422.41, extending a strong two-week rally of 9.15%. The stock is riding a wave of elevated oil refining economics: crude prices are holding firm (US oil at $107/barrel, world prices at $130.80), refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, and diesel supplies are tight enough to command record prices. Today's move likely reflects the market digesting that these high energy costs—which squeeze most industries—actually boost refiner margins, the profit spread between what they pay for crude and what they sell refined products for.

The broader geopolitical backdrop is also tilting refiner-friendly right now. News that Saudi Arabia is offering more crude through the Strait of Hormuz after a pipeline attack, and signals from Trump that the US may be nearing the end of its Iran tensions, have eased some of the acute supply-disruption fears that spiked prices higher in recent weeks. That stability at elevated price levels—rather than a crash back down—is the sweet spot for refiners: strong margins without the chaos of war-driven volatility.
